newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Doctor sees Mobutu over hospital treatment in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Doctor sees Mobutu over hospital treatment in Morocco.

text.p: The ousted leader of former Zaire, President Mobutu Sese Seko, is to enter hospital soon in the north Moroccan town of Tangier for chemotherapy treatment for his prostate cancer, hospital sources said on Thursday.
"No date has been set yet. The hospital medical director went to see him at 11 a.m. today," one medical source in Tangier's Mohamed V hospital told Reuters by telephone.
"It is envisaged he will be admitted but there's no date yet."
Mobutu, ousted last month after a seven-month-long rebellion following three decades in power, has been suffering from prostate cancer for which he had extensive treatment in Europe.

He arrived in Morocco with an entourage of around 30 people, including family, on May 23, taking up residence at the 30-room Amphitrite Hotel next door to King Hassan's royal palace of Skhirat, 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat.
On Wednesday he moved to the north Morocco sea resort at Cap Spartel, north of Tangier, where he is expected to spend up to six weeks.
A worker at Le Mirage Hotel at the resort told Reuters on Wednesday: "King Hassan's guest (Mobutu) arrived at the hotel this afternoon with his family."
The source would give no other details.
Earlier on Wednesday a manager in Le Mirage said: "Mobutu and his entourage are expected to spend several weeks here...All hotel rooms have been requisitioned until August 20."
There was heavy security around the hotel, witnesses said.
